title: Recover interrupted record transactions without guessing or replaying decisions
statement: The system shall recover an explicitly selected interrupted current-format record transaction only by restoring its verified before-state or completing its exact prepared candidate, preserving foreign content and stopping on unavailable, tampered, incompatible, or unrecognized recovery state.

what.problem: An interruption can leave incomplete publication; guessed repair or replay against newer state can create decisions never supplied by the actor or overwrite unrelated work.
what.desired_outcome: An operator obtains an exact attributable terminal state or a safe recovery stop while retaining enough valid information for subsequent recovery.

why.rationale: Recoverability must protect both recorded engineering meaning and acknowledged successful work.

stakeholders: Engineers and reviewers operating on recorded engineering work
Engineering agents acting on explicit actor decisions
Maintainers and consumers of the published command-line interface

conditions: After an interrupted save, during explicitly requested restore or complete, and when recovery itself is interrupted.

contexts: One selected supported transaction and its exact before/candidate snapshots, target identities, and declared read basis.

how.approach: Validate the explicit transaction selector and expected recovery identity, the current journal/version, and exact snapshots. Require targets to match before or candidate state at observed checks. Complete only with fresh declared basis; restore verified before bytes; never rerun targeted semantic operations against a new state.

how_much.scope: Current v3 recovery only, under the same local containment and observed external-edit limits as publication. Retired or mixed journal/state selectors have no conversion or compatibility repair path. Recovery concerns a transaction, not general historical-baseline restoration.

acceptance_criteria: Missing, corrupt, tampered, unsupported, or mixed recovery information stops without guessed repair; observed target bytes matching neither before nor candidate state stop without overwriting that third state.

Complete publishes the exact prepared candidate only with verified snapshots and unchanged declared reads. Restore uses verified before snapshots without changing external basis files or fabricating new decisions.

Acknowledged committed transactions permit completion/cleanup but not rollback of saved success. Restoring initial creation removes only transaction-created content and empty created directories, preserving preexisting or externally added content.

Recovery can be interrupted and retried with refreshed recovery identity while remaining recoverable; verified terminal recovery may clean private snapshots without treating them as workflow evidence.
Ordinary reads, check, preview, discovery, and diagnostic lookup perform no implicit recovery. Retired history remains byte-preserved and operationally unsupported.
